ratings.note: 76% 1-star. Skewed by billing complaints (charged after cancelling, annual renewals) and support. There are also some complaints about prompt-following and distorted output. 93 reviews in the last 12 months. Star graphic shows 1.5, number shows 1.7.

Most reviews predate V8: the newest is about 6 months old, the oldest about 3 years. Praise is for polished stylised output for concept art and moodboards. Complaints are limited control, character consistency, price, the Discord workflow and billing.

vendor_claims.text: V8.1 renders standard jobs roughly 4-5x faster than earlier versions, with native 2K output (reported by third-party write-ups of Midjourney's announcement).

strengths: default aesthetic and style exploration for concept art (consensus of desk reviews)
consistent visual style across a set
weaknesses: weaker prompt adherence and in-image text than the API leaders
no official public API; no free plan
Trustpilot dominated by billing and cancellation complaints
midjourney.notes: Current default is V8.2 (since 2026-07-24, per several secondary sources). Midjourney is NOT on the Artificial Analysis or LMArena boards (no public API), so it has no benchmark evidence. Every review found is either a desk summary or written by a reseller or competitor; I verified no independent hands-on same-prompt test within the search budget. The desk consensus that Midjourney leads on concept-art aesthetics is strong and unanimous, but it does not meet the hands-on rule.

benchmarks.source: Artificial Analysis text-to-image arena (AA-Image-T2I v2.1, Overall)
benchmarks.note: Sunburst (max) is #1 at 1222 (percentile 100). I credit Flare because it is the API default, and a hands-on report suggests it is ChatGPT's default variant, though OpenAI hasn't confirmed this. GPT Image 2 (high) is #3 (1186). No style or game-art sub-board exists.
arena.ai returned 403, so the figures come from a third-party mirror and are unverified at source. Marked preliminary. Sunburst is #1 at 1425.

reviews.author: Alexander Weipprecht

reviews.author: DevToolLab Team
reviews.summary: Called the safest default for general generation and editing, with no art-specific verdict.

ratings.note: Covers all of ChatGPT (mostly chat, limits, billing and support), not image generation specifically. A few reviews complain about image edits and guardrails. I recommend NOT scoring it for concept-art.

mentions.note: Hands-on users praise reference-following and speed. Complaints: hands/anatomy, detail loss on edits, 'ChatGPT look' sameness; 'still can't make sprite sheets'; pixel-art models do better. I read only the first ~100k of 212k characters.

Leans negative. Praise for prompt adherence; complaints about anatomy in crowds, counting/grid failures, pixel-art requests coming back with too many colours, and sameness. Previous model. Only the first ~100k of 390k characters read.

vendor_claims.text: Images 2.5 (2026-09-08) claims up to 50% lower latency than Images 2.0, with better lighting, textures and subject preservation; it adds Sketch, Templates and comment-based edits (as reported by press).

strengths: tops both Artificial Analysis image boards (generation and editing)
weaknesses: sprite sheets and true low-colour pixel art still weak (HN users)
'sameness' / recognisable house style; less expressive than Midjourney
chatgpt.notes: OpenAI says GPT Image 2.5 is available to all ChatGPT users (free and paid, per press). ChatGPT shows one model; the API splits it into Flare (default) and Sunburst. OpenAI has not confirmed which variant ChatGPT uses (MindStudio: https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/gpt-image-25-pricing-access). Both variants are #1/#2, so the choice barely changes the score. No independent hands-on art review of 2.5 was found.

It also resells third-party models: FLUX (Dev, Kontext pro, Flux.2 Kontext Pro, Schnell), Seedream 4.0/4.5, Nano Banana / Nano Banana Pro and GPT Image 1.5 (docs snapshot updated 2026-01-23: https://docs.leonardo.ai/v1.0/docs/list-of-models). Third-party models it hosts (e.g. Nano Banana Pro at AA #11) are not credited.

scenario.notes: MULTI-MODEL PLATFORM / RESELLER. Scenario makes no base image model of its own. Custom models are LoRA-style trainings on Flux 2, Z-Image, Qwen Image and similar bases. It hosts GPT Image 2/2.5, Nano Banana 2/Pro, Seedream 4.5/5.0 Lite and Retro Diffusion models, among others (Scenario help pages, from search snippets; not opened directly). No benchmark is creditable to Scenario. G2 returned 403. I found no independent hands-on review.

caveats: 1) The web search budget ran out partway through, so side tools (Skybox AI, Sloyd, Unity AI, Dreamlands) got almost no research, and I couldn't look for independent hands-on Midjourney V8.x tests from major outlets (Tom's Guide, TechRadar, Creative Bloq) or YouTube same-prompt comparisons. 2) Almost every 2026 'comparison' found is a desk summary built from docs and leaderboards, or comes from a reseller or competitor (Nolvia, Pixmax, NemoVideo, Ludo, Sprite AI, Cinevva). These are recorded with hands_on/independent flags and score_recommended=false. The only scoreable independent hands-on review is Techsy's PixelLab walk-cycle test. 3) Midjourney has no benchmark (absent from both arenas), and its user ratings conflict: Trustpilot 1.7 (billing-driven) vs Product Hunt 4.7 (mostly pre-V8). 4) For ChatGPT, OpenAI hasn't confirmed which GPT Image 2.5 variant it uses; Flare is credited, and Sunburst would give 100 instead of ~99. 5) Leonardo, Scenario and Layer resell third-party models; only Leonardo's own Lucid Origin is credited. Scenario and Layer have no creditable benchmark. 6) LMArena figures are from a third-party mirror, not verified at source. 7) Reddit and X were skipped by instruction. HN had usable threads only for ChatGPT (2 read, partially), below the 3-thread minimum. 8) The PixelLab vs Retro Diffusion academic benchmark is unverified: the paper wasn't found, and the only account comes from Retro Diffusion's developer.
